Let’s talk about something that’s at the heart of freedom—truth and language.
Authoritarian regimes, throughout history, have relied on twisting the truth and warping the words we use. When facts get fuzzy and language loses its meaning, those in power can shape public opinion and justify almost anything they do. That’s why standing up for objective reality and clear communication is absolutely essential if we want to push back against tyranny.
One of the first moves authoritarian leaders make is to chip away at trust in independent sources of information. Think about how often the press is attacked, conspiracy theories are spread, or misinformation floods your social media feed. When you’re left unsure about what’s real and what’s not, it gets way easier for propaganda to slip in and take hold.
But it’s not just about the facts—it’s about the words we use, too. Language can be turned into a weapon. Clichés, euphemisms, and catchy slogans can actually hide the ugly side of certain policies or actions. Imagine hearing vague phrases that gloss over acts of violence or discrimination—it can make them sound almost normal, or even acceptable. And after a while, it gets harder for people to spot injustice, let alone stand up to it.
So, how do you push back? It starts with building the habit of searching for reliable information and thinking critically about what you read or hear. Don’t just stick with news from one place—find trustworthy sources, check the facts, and even challenge your own assumptions every now and then. And pay attention to how language is being used around you. If someone’s using words that seem meant to soften or cover up the truth, don’t let it slide.
Here are a few practical ways you can defend truth and language in your daily life:
Be kind to language. Use clear, honest words, and steer clear of clichés that hide what’s really going on.
Believe in truth. Stand up for the idea that real, objective facts exist—and they matter.
Investigate. Go after reliable information, and always double-check before you accept something as true.
Listen for dangerous words. Stay alert for language that makes oppression or violence sound reasonable.
When you insist on clarity and honesty, you help create a space where propaganda finds it much harder to take root. And in that kind of environment, it’s a whole lot tougher for authoritarian leaders to tighten their grip on power.
